seven_q.Q0_posture: This document takes a posture of formal analysis, seeking structural parallels between two domains without claiming material identity.
seven_q.Q1_identity: This is an isomorphism record (ISO-029) documenting a structural mapping between music theory and Trinitarian theology.
seven_q.Q2_domain: It lives at the intersection of music theory, Christian theology, acoustic physics, and philosophy of mathematics.
seven_q.Q3_claim: The harmonic series and triadic harmony exhibit the same generative topology as the Trinity: single source, perfect image, dynamic mover, minimum three for completeness, and gravitational attraction toward source.
seven_q.Q4_support: Support comes from 10 independent correspondences, formal models (Lerdahl, Helmholtz), scriptural references, and historical theological sources (Augustine, Boethius).
seven_q.Q5_dependencies: Depends on the harmonic series as a physical fact, Lerdahl's tonal pitch space, Nicene Trinitarian theology, and the concept of structural isomorphism.
seven_q.Q6_consequences: Forces that any theology with fewer or more than three persons is structurally incomplete or redundant; that worship without tonal center degrades; that dissonance requires costly resolution.
seven_q.Q7_kill: Would be killed by demonstrating two pitch classes suffice for complete harmonic function, or by producing a coherent Binitarian theology, or by showing the generative topology does not match.
